about.text: I am a Ph.D. student at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, supervised by Prof. Michael R. Lyu. My research focuses on AI 4 Infra & Infra 4 AI: building high-performance infrastructure for AI workloads (LLM inference and serving systems, GPU/accelerator systems, multi-GPU scheduling), and applying AI to make cloud and LLM-as-a-Service platforms fast, reliable, and operable.

publications.title: SimServing: Native-Execution Simulation for Evolution-Resilient LLM Serving Configuration Tuning
publications.authors: **Yujie Huang**, Jiazhen Gu, Zhihan Jiang, Michael R. Lyu
publications.venueFull: The IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
publications.abstract: SimServing executes the original serving framework while substituting GPU computation with latency estimates, avoiding the maintenance drift of separately implemented simulators. Combined with particle swarm optimization, it supports efficient configuration search. Evaluation reduces throughput prediction error from 13.8% to 4.9%, accelerates simulation by up to 21.18 times, and finds configurations with up to 10.2% higher throughput.

publications.title: LLMGuard: Multi-Agent Fault Diagnosis for Reliable Language-Model-as-a-Service
publications.authors: Yuedong Zhong, Guangba Yu, **Yujie Huang**, Qunchao Fu, Rui Ren, Cong Feng, Yongqiang Yang, Michael R. Lyu
publications.venueFull: The IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Dependable Systems and Networks
publications.abstract: LLMGuard diagnoses failures in large LMaaS deployments through a deterministic multi-agent workflow. It compiles troubleshooting procedures into a checking tree, verifies candidate causes, prunes unsupported branches, and records an evidence chain. Experiments on production infrastructure with more than 10,000 accelerators demonstrate improved diagnosis accuracy and identification times measured in seconds.

publications.title: StaR: Stateful Dynamic-Graph Root Cause Analysis through Memory-Enhanced Causality Discovery
publications.authors: Haiyu Huang, Derek Ng, Jiewei Lyu, **Yujie Huang**, Guangba Yu, Yilun Wang, Michael R. Lyu
publications.venueFull: The 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
publications.abstract: StaR investigates root causes in multivariate time-series systems whose dependencies change over time. It combines temporal memory, message passing, and neural Granger causality to track evolving states and discover causal relationships. Its implementation supports dynamic graphs and evaluates both root cause localization and causal discovery on synthetic and real-world datasets.

publications.title: PreServe: Intelligent Management for LMaaS Systems via Hierarchical Prediction
publications.authors: Zhihan Jiang, **Yujie Huang**, Guangba Yu, Junjie Huang, Jiazhen Gu, Michael R. Lyu
publications.venueFull: The IEEE/ACM International Conference on Software Engineering
publications.abstract: PreServe manages LMaaS resources by combining forecasts of service-wide workload with estimates of individual request demand. Per-instance predictions guide proactive scaling and request routing, balancing present and expected load. Production-data experiments report 41.3% lower tail latency and 49.38% lower resource consumption, with an additional overhead of 0.23%.
citationTitleAliases: Hierarchical Prediction-based Management for LMaaS Systems

publications.title: LLMPrism: Black-box Performance Diagnosis for Production LLM Training Platforms
publications.authors: Zhihan Jiang, Rui Ren, Guangba Yu, Yulun Wu, Wenwei Gu, Yichen Li, **Yujie Huang**, Cong Feng, Zengyin Yang, Yongqiang Yang, Michael R. Lyu
publications.venueFull: The IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Dependable Systems and Networks, Industry Track
publications.abstract: LLMPrism monitors training performance from network traffic without modifying training jobs. It identifies jobs and parallelism strategies, reconstructs execution timelines, and uses those timelines to diagnose performance problems. Production deployment demonstrates continuous, lightweight monitoring and timeline reconstruction error within 0.3%, addressing the limited visibility available to multi-tenant platform operators.

publications.title: Why Does the LLM Stop Computing: An Empirical Study of User-Reported Failures in Open-Source LLMs
publications.authors: Guangba Yu, Zirui Wang, **Yujie Huang**, Renyi Zhong, Yuedong Zhong, Yilun Wang, Michael R. Lyu
publications.abstract: This study examines 705 reported failures across DeepSeek, Llama, and Qwen deployments. It identifies shared reliability problems in the surrounding software and infrastructure, distinguishes crash-related infrastructure friction from tokenizer-related functional defects, and traces how barriers shift between fine-tuning and inference. The released dataset supports further work on dependable self-managed LLM deployment.
publications.venueFull: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology

publications.title: Cloud-OpsBench: A Reproducible Benchmark for Agentic Root Cause Analysis in Cloud Systems
publications.authors: Yilun Wang, Guangba Yu, Haiyu Huang, Zirui Wang, **Yujie Huang**, Pengfei Chen, Michael R. Lyu
publications.abstract: Cloud-OpsBench evaluates cloud root cause analysis through reproducible incident snapshots and interactive diagnostic interfaces. It contains 754 verified cases spanning 57 fault types, with evidence graphs for examining investigation quality. Evaluation of eleven language models shows that correct final diagnoses can still lack sufficient supporting evidence, motivating assessment of both outcomes and diagnostic process.
